label: thm:path
title: Weighted pseudorandom generators with improved error dependence for general ordered branching programs
work: Pseudodistributions That Beat All Pseudorandom Generators
difficulty_reason: The new obligation constructs weighted pseudorandomness for general ordered branching programs with improved error dependence. The complete human proof expresses the path-Laplacian inverse by Richardson iteration, compresses a cancellation-structured sum of matrix products, and implements its weighted outputs with the inner INW generator under explicit space bounds. Those interacting inverse-error, indexed cancellation and generator-compression arguments form a substantive new research core; the Richardson identity and standard INW generator are attributed supporting prerequisites.
required_context: Full source definitions 906–1020, path-Laplacian and weak-error bounds, exact Richardson identity 580–583 and 1155–1157, and complete new construction 1032–1308 retained. Only original Theorem4.1 selected, with all intermediate statements as support; permutation-branching and sampler branches held/unselected.
scope_text: Prove the authors' general ordered-branching-program WPRG theorem, original Theorem 4.1. The path-Laplacian inverse, weak-error and inverse-norm bounds, complete Richardson identity with exponent m+1, explicit iteration count, all indexed summand cancellations and the inner-INW weighted-output/space construction are retained. The full article and bibliography form conservative context; the distinct permutation-branching and sampler results are unselected and remain under separate source-scope holds. Supporting intermediate statements are uncounted.
disclosure_text: The original Lemma 4.9 (native lines 1163–1176; original PDF page 23) promises \(\eps/2\), while its terminal displayed proof bound is literally \(\eps(n+1)/(2n)\). Both are preserved, together with the author's exact Richardson identity, exponent \(m+1\), iteration count \(\ell=\lceil\log_n(1/\eps)\rceil+1\), and all weak-error/inverse-norm bounds. The selected primary is the authored asymptotic seed-length construction. The original theorem quantifies \(n\in\N\) and uses \(\log_n\); no separate \(n=1\) interpretation was found in the retained source, and none is supplied editorially. No inequality, error rescaling or iteration count is changed.
